messages.subject: shinyAce problems with some versions of shiny-server?
parts:
Related to my app mentioned here:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/57qm574qGIU

( The app is here: http://spark.rstudio.com/uafsnap/plot3D/ )

this bug/issue is sufficiently different to warrant a different thread. Switching from shiny-server 0.3.3 to 1.0.0.42 leads to a case where any of my apps which use shinyAce to display highlighted code do not work properly. I know my context is particular. I have UI elements that allow the user to change the syntax highlighting theme or font size via updateAceEditor. Works great on my Windows PC where I initially create an app, and seemingly as well on Spark where it ultimately ends up, but I tend to really test an app at a middle stage on our own hosting of shiny-server before deploying to Spark because I can't count on what works on my Windows PC with localhost to always work on a server.

What I find with shiny-server 1.0.0.42 is that none of the buttons or menus throughout the entire app UI will build at launch if I am trying to display the .R files for my app with shinyAce in the main panel area. It kind of reminds me of what I might see happen with the UI if I accidentally reference the same uiOutputs multiple times, resulting in lots of things missing from the app when I try to run it. None of that is going here though, and it all works well on PC and on Spark. I have to comment out various references to displaying highlighted code as reactive output elements. Then the app builds properly again and is functional. The odd thing is I don't have to comment out all my R scripts I want to show code for, only some of them, and not the same ones from one app to another.

I'll try my best here to display some relevant snippets of code. The structure is a little opaque, I know. It is very cool on the systems it works on, but also quite the edge case perhaps.

It begins in the global.R file where I obtain the names and paths of my .R files in my app and initialize with aceEditor:
library(shinyAce)
R_files <- paste0(c( # vector of .R file names
"global", "ui", "server",
file.path("external", c("app", "sidebar", "main", "about")),
file.path("external/appSourceFiles", c(paste0("io.sidebar.wp", 1:6), "reactives"))
), ".R")

showCode <- function(file, ht="600px"){ # content to eventually display in app
list(
h4(HTML(basename(file))),
aceEditor(gsub('\\.', '', basename(file)), value=paste(readLines(file), collapse='\n'), mode='r', height=ht, readOnly=TRUE)
)
}
for(i in 1:length(R_files)) assign(paste0("show_", gsub("\\.R", "R", basename(R_files[i]))), showCode(R_files[i])) # create the above list object for each R file

Inside the call to sidebarPanel() I will have a conditional panel that only shows when on the 'R Code' tab in the mainPanel area. It looks like this:

conditionalPanel(condition="input.tsp==='rcode'",
navlistPanel(
"Top-level Code",
tabPanel("Global", value="nlp_globalR"),
tabPanel("UI", value="nlp_uiR"),
tabPanel("Server", value="nlp_serverR"),
"Mid-level Code",
tabPanel("App", value="nlp_appR"),
tabPanel("Header", value="nlp_headerR"),
tabPanel("Sidebar", value="nlp_sidebarR"),
tabPanel("Main", value="nlp_mainR"),
tabPanel("About", value="nlp_aboutR"),
"Bottom-level Code",
tabPanel("Well Panel 1", value="nlp_io.sidebar.wp1R"),
tabPanel("Well Panel 2", value="nlp_io.sidebar.wp2R"),
tabPanel("Reactives", value="nlp_reactivesR"),
id="nlp",
widths=c(12,1)
),
div(class="row-fluid",
div(class="span6", uiOutput("HLTheme")),
div(class="span6", uiOutput("HLFontSize"))
)
)

where "HLTheme" and "HLFontSize" are inside the call to shinyServer:

output$HLTheme <- renderUI({ selectInput("hltheme", "Code highlighting theme:", getAceThemes(), selected="clouds_midnight") })
output$HLFontSize <- renderUI({ selectInput("hlfontsize", "Font size:", seq(8,24,by=2), selected=12) })

where I also update the display of the app's .R files with updateAceEditor:
observe({
input$tsp
input$nlp
input$hltheme
for(i in 1:length(R_files)) eval(parse(text=sprintf("input$%s", gsub("\\.", "", basename(R_files[i])))))
for(i in 1:length(R_files)) updateAceEditor(session, gsub("\\.", "", basename(R_files[i])), theme=input$hltheme, fontSize=input$hlfontsize)
})

This navlistPanel doesn't display outputs. I simply reference its value via input$nlp later. Finally, there is the mainPanel which includes the R Code tabPanel:

tabPanel("R Code",
conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_aboutR'", show_aboutR), # Each line refers to the navlistPanel current ID and then displays the content defined in global.R
conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_appR'", show_appR),
conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_globalR'", show_globalR),
#conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_headerR'", show_headerR),
#conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_io.sidebar.wp1R'", show_io.sidebar.wp1R),
#conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_io.sidebar.wp2R'", show_io.sidebar.wp2R),
#conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_io.sidebar.wp3R'", show_io.sidebar.wp3R),
#conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_io.sidebar.wp4R'", show_io.sidebar.wp4R),
#conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_io.sidebar.wp5R'", show_io.sidebar.wp5R),
#conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_io.sidebar.wp6R'", show_io.sidebar.wp6R),
#conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_mainR'", show_mainR),
#conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_reactivesR'", show_reactivesR),
#conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_serverR'", show_serverR),
#conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_sidebarR'", show_sidebarR),
conditionalPanel(condition="input.nlp==='nlp_uiR'", show_uiR),
value="rcode"),
id="tsp"
)

Notice that all but the first three and the last one are commented out, to prevent them from displaying in the tabPanel in the browser. This is what I have to do for the app to work with shiny-server. I can include the files if using Spark though, or just a PC. With shiny-server 1.0.0.42 inclusion of any one of the commented out lines leads to the UI having all its menus missing. This did not happen at least with version 0.3.3.

I understand this is not a straightforward or simple application of shiny or shinyAce to construct this kind of conditional reactive usage. However, it does work on other systems just fine, and I do not see any reason why it shouldn't. But given the complexity, I don't really like asking anyone to look at this. If there is a better way I can present this kind of edge case please let me know and I will do my best.

Thanks,
Matt

messages.subject: Re: shinyAce problems with some versions of shiny-server?
parts:
You're right; there are a lot of moving pieces in here. I don't have any concrete epiphanies, but maybe a couple of things to check:
  • File permissions. Do the necessary users have read access to all the referenced files? If not, R might throw an error which could potentially cause some of the renderUIs() to be blank or errant. 
  • Maybe try whittling down the number of variables here by just printing or writing the output to a file instead of sending it to ShinyAce. That would allow you to test the different pieces in isolation which might help narrow things down. Ultimately, it's possible there's a bug in one of the underlying systems but none of us would know unless we had a minimally reproducible example showing the issue so we could track it down.
  • Have you seen Shiny's new "Showcase Mode"? (e.g. http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/telephones-by-region.html). It sounds like that offers at least some of what you're trying to build.

Good luck! Let us know if you're able to narrow it down a little further. Ideally, if you can pare the code down to a few dozen lines and post it in a Gist, that would make it a lot easier for someone externally to dig into the issue.

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: shinyAce problems with some versions of shiny-server?
parts:
Hi Jeff,

I have narrowed this down to two distinct issues.
(1) There were some files permissions changes I needed to make:
chgrp -R shiny plot3D/
chmod -R g+rwX plot3D/

This was interesting because I only use shinyAce to show code from files needed for the app to run. The shiny user has no problem reading these to run the app. But with shinyAce I needed to explicitly add the shiny group (we set this group up for our server). Until now I have only had to add the shiny group so that the shiny user could use my files if I was making an app that was for the specific purpose of writing files or executing other processes on other servers behind our firewall. This permissions change cleared up all the problems but one. This is comforting because the one .R script that, if I attempt to display with shinyAce, leads to the whole UI not building its reactive elements (buttons, menus, etc) is now common to both versions of shiny-server I have used.

(2) My header.R file. I have confirmed further that it is only a problem if my header file contains a Google Analytics tracking code script. The app works fine with GA, and I can track my app usage on Spark with it. It is useless on our private server of course but simply appears in the code because it's an intermediate location where I develop the app. I just can't have that snippet in there and use shinyAce to display it without breaking the app. I've attached both versions of the script, very small. Maybe there is some rule in shiny or shinyAce about not displaying certain types of code.

I am very excited about Showcase Mode! It is really cool. I have not used it yet. Many of my apps use code externalization to keep my code organized, with a hierarchy of files sourcing other files. This has helped me build apps somewhat more generally and use one app as a template for the next even as the apps become increasingly complex. I thought about Showcase mode, but I figured as awesome as it would be for the user to be able to see the code that is running highlighted in real-time, if I have an app that consists of ten R scripts, the user seeing anything at all is contingent upon them being on the right script tab and scrolled to the right position in the script. So at least for more complex apps with many files, for the time being using the navlist panel struck me as the cleanest way to organize my code for display, though I do really love the idea of that Showcase reactivity. I also thought Showcase Mode was only available through ShinyApps.io. Is that not the case?

Thanks,
Matt

messages.subject: Re: shinyAce problems with some versions of shiny-server?
parts:
Hi Jeff,

I have some additional helpful information. Today with the help of our IT person we were able to figure out that the issue was not entirely solved by fixing some file permissions, or the type of code being displayed (my header.R example). There was at least a third issue.

This actually relates the shinyAce issue here to my prior thread about the rgl issue where you mentioned WebSocket. On our private hosting of shiny-server v1.0.0.42, there remain problems for some apps showing code with shinyAce even after accounting for other issues such as file permissions. But once I use Ctrl-Alt-Shift-A to turn off WebSocket and reload the app, this problem completely goes away and everything displays fine. So WebSocket actually cannot be on for shinyAce to be used at least in the style it is used in the app referenced here.

Ironically, this is the same app using rgl and shinyRGL packages, where having it off may be an issue for the rgl plots. I must note though since uncovering the need to turn off WebSocket for shinyAce in this context, controlling for that issue I am not able to get the app to crash with WebSocket off when making the rgl plots as happens on Spark. So WebSocket clearly is an issue with my use of Ace but NOT necessarily for rgl.

Matt
